If a pointer claims coverage, repoint it to the active row that now carries the content; if it is history, mark it '(switched off)'. Notes only, your own segment only.

Scrub-trimmed clauses (SOP rule 78 with rule 47; found at NJ's retro sync, 2026-09-30): the 2026-09-29 scrub shortened `late-fee-limit-va`, `acceptable-payment-methods-va`, `casualty-termination-va`, moving statutory limits into education. For each, check whether the trimmed clause, filled with a lawful-looking landlord figure or choice, can now break a statutory limit or condition for any tenant (a protected group's grace period, a notice rule, a condition the statute attaches). Caps a number check can catch are the builder's job (backlog M.13); conditions it can't catch belong back in the clause. NJ restored the 2A:42-6.1 senior and benefit-recipient grace period to `late-fee-nj` this way. Restore only what is needed, and record the verdict for each clause. Also check whether the scrub removed text a statute requires in the lease itself, from these clauses or any other the scrub shortened: search the state's required-content provisions, not only each clause's own citation (SOP rule 78; CO's retro, 2026-10-01, found `habitability-notice-co` stripped of the warranty and no-retaliation statements C.R.S. § 38-12-505(3)(c) requires in every lease).

Scrub-switched-off required clauses (SOP rule 78 with rule 46; found at AZ's retro sync, 2026-09-30): the 2026-09-29 scrub switched off `security-deposit-return-va`, which were marked REQUIRED or CONDITIONAL, moving their content to education. For each, check whether a statute requires a written notice or disclosure that this lease clause was carrying (given in the lease, or in writing at signing or move-in). If so, restore a lease clause as that notice (AZ restored its A.R.S. § 33-1321(C) move-out-inspection notice as `move-out-inspection-notice-az`); if the clause only restated a right the law gives anyway, record that. Record the verdict for each.

Rule 62 vetting, shared rows (queued at the CA retro sync, 2026-10-03; answer each, shared text not edited): (1) `surrender-end-of-term` (CA's proposal, 2026-10-03): qualify 'Tenant will surrender possession of the property and return all keys to Landlord immediately' with 'unless applicable law entitles Tenant to remain', because a just-cause or similar statute may let a tenant stay past the term. Is the qualified wording lawful and accurate in your state, and does the current wording state a duty your law doesn't back? (2) `default-by-tenant` (MN's proposal, 2026-10-02; ND and CA support): move the no-cure carve-out ('except where applicable law permits Landlord to proceed without giving Tenant an opportunity to cure') out of the non-rent limb into its own sentence reaching both limbs. Is that lawful and accurate in your state (it is self-limiting, so check only that it can't be read to drop a cure or pre-suit notice your law requires for nonpayment)? Already settled, so don't ask Taylor again: if the edit would only drop the lease's own promise of written notice of a rent default that your law doesn't require, Taylor decided for Indiana (2026-10-03) and Pennsylvania (2026-10-04) that the lease follows the statute, with no optional notice clause. Support the edit, and say in your section which education row should tell landlords they may still give notice first (Claude Code updates it at the merge).
